title: Yucatán Achiote Pollo Asado Spread
seoTitle: Yucatán Achiote Pollo Asado Spread | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Pollo asado recado night—sour orange achiote char, not chipotle fajita repeat
subtitle: Yucatán recado rojo leg quarters, sour orange, and charred jicama for ten
description: Chicken leg quarters marinate in sour orange, recado rojo, and annatto, griddle until skin crisps and 175°F, and serve with charred jicama and habanero salsa.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Yucatán Achiote Pollo Asado Spread in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Build recado marinade
steps.instruction: Blend sour orange, recado rojo, annatto, chicken fat, allspice, and epazote until smooth. Coat leg quarters and marinate 4–12 hours. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Preheat grill grates
steps.instruction: Preheat grill to medium, 400°F. Oil grates for skin-on chicken. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill skin-side down
steps.instruction: Grill leg quarters skin-side down 15 minutes undisturbed until skin crisps and releases. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Flip and finish
steps.instruction: Flip and grill 15–18 minutes until 175°F internal and juices run clear. Move to indirect if flare-ups. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill radishes
steps.instruction: Grill radish halves 3 minutes per side at 425°F until charred and slightly softened. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and hold
steps.instruction: Rest chicken 5 minutes. Hold covered at 170°F in hotel pans. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Warm tortillas
steps.instruction: Wrap tortillas in foil and warm on grill 3 minutes at 350°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Platter for ten
steps.instruction: Family-style platters with chicken, radishes, tortillas, and cilantro. One leg quarter plus thigh per person. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Achiote stains everything—wear gloves when blending marinade.
Skin-side down first is non-negotiable for crisp pollo asado.
175°F for dark meat; white-meat rules don't apply to leg quarters.
tonightSpread: Pollo asado citrus platter with grilled radish and tortillas.
Black beans with lime on the side.
leftovers: Pull meat for citrus chicken tacos.
Chop into pozole-style soup with hominy.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Yucatecan pollo asado brings recado depth—not peri-peri, not chipotle lime. Leg quarters stay juicy on the flat-top and hold covered at 170°F for shift meals.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate 4–12 hours. Griddle medium 400°F skin-side down first, 35 minutes total. Hold covered at 170°F up to 40 minutes. Jicama chars last 6 minutes.
